html:
Multan is an old city on the Chenab River in the Punjab, today in Pakistan. On the 900 and 1783 maps it is a state or province of its own between Sindh and the upper Punjab.

The city was famous for its sun temple, which drew pilgrims from across India; see the Multan Sun Temple. The Arabs took it in 713, after the conquest of Sindh, and kept the temple as a source of income. By the 9th century Arab emirs ruled Multan on their own, and in the 10th century it came under Ismaili Shia rulers loyal to the Fatimid Caliphate. Mahmud of Ghazni crushed them in the early 1000s.

Later Multan was ruled from Delhi, then by the local Langah Sultanate, then as a province of the Mughal Empire. On the 1783 map it is held by the Afghans of the Durrani Empire, founded by Ahmad Shah Durrani. In 1818 Ranjit Singh took it for the Sikhs.
sum: Multan is an old city on the Chenab River in the Punjab, today in Pakistan. On the 900 and 1783 maps it is a state or province of its own between Sindh and the upper Punjab.
